blocks.raw: <Note>When you encounter a planning question on the LEA, your first move should be to identify the sclea it is operating at. A question about lot coverage is a site-planning question. A question about CLUP approval is a governance question. A question about TOD is an urban-planning question. Identifying the sclea focuses your recall.</Note>

blocks.raw: <ExamTip>Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA), required under PD 1586, operates across scleas — from the site (direct impacts) to the regional (cumulative and downstream impacts). Understanding EIA as a multi-sclea tool connects site planning, environmental design, and governance in one framework.</ExamTip>

blocks.raw: <Tip>The connection between planning and design is most visible in the site plan — the drawing that shows a building in its site context, with setbacks, landscaping, parking, access drives, and open space all shown. If you are comfortable reading and drawing site plans, you are already thinking across the planning-design boundary.</Tip>
